learning_objective: 🎯 Journey into the microscopic world to understand atomic models, electron orbits, and the specific colors of light atoms emit!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: By firing alpha particles at a thin gold foil, Rutherford proved that most of an atom is entirely empty space, with almost all its mass and positive charge concentrated in a tiny, dense center called the Nucleus.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🪐 Bohr Model of the Hydrogen Atom
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Bohr fixed Rutherford's model by stating that electrons don't just orbit anywhere; they exist in specific, 'quantized' stable orbits without radiating energy. They only emit or absorb light when jumping between these orbits.
Bohr's masterstroke: The electron's angular momentum is quantized as an integral multiple of $h/2\pi$ ($L = nh/2\pi$). This is why only specific orbits are allowed.

Electrons have negative total energy because they are bound to the nucleus. For Hydrogen, the energy in the $n$-th orbit is $E_n = -13.6/n^2 \text{ eV}$. To jump up, they absorb a photon. To fall down, they emit a photon.

When excited Hydrogen electrons fall to lower orbits, they emit light of very specific wavelengths. These lines are grouped into series: Lyman (falls to $n=1$, UV), Balmer (falls to $n=2$, Visible), Paschen (falls to $n=3$, Infrared).

fun_activity.title: 🏙️ Neon Sign Science
fun_activity.instructions: Look at colorful neon signs at night. A true 'Neon' sign only glows red-orange. Other colors use different gases. The electric current excites the gas atoms, and as their electrons fall back to stable orbits, they emit specific colors of the spectrum!

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize the regions of the spectrum for Hydrogen: Lyman is Ultraviolet, Balmer is Visible, and Paschen, Brackett, and Pfund are Infrared.
📌 Know how to calculate the wavelength of an emitted photon using Rydberg's formula ($1/\lambda = R(1/n_f^2 - 1/n_i^2)$).
📌 Bohr's model is only successful for hydrogen-like (single-electron) atoms/ions (like $He^+$, $Li^{2+}$).
quick_recap: ⭐ Electrons are like people on a staircase; they can stand on step 1 or step 2, but never in between.
⭐ The Balmer series is the only part of the hydrogen spectrum visible to the human eye.
